text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming.sse.p99 latency 5.2s (SLO=1.0s) across prod-us-west and prod-eu. auto-paging oncall=ryan.oncall. potential customer impact: playback stalls / delayed chunk delivery. links: https://grafana.redwood/streaming/slo?panel=p99 , https://logs.redwood/streaming?filter=504

ryan.oncall: acked. I'm on it, joining traces now. any recent deploys affecting proxy or streaming runtime?

maria.sre: I saw spike in tail latency around 15:07 UTC, coincides with increased connection churn from mobile clients (long-poll fallback). p95 is ~1.2s but p99 exploded.

siva.eng: rolling deploy to streaming-proxy happened ~14:52 (rev a3f1b2). I pushed a config tweak for keepalive earlier today but no restart then.

anya.support: a couple of customers reported 'stuttering' in chat widgets and intermittent hangs. CX ticket 3421 opened.

ryan.oncall: quick triage steps: 1) check envoy/nginx 504 rate 2) check streaming worker error logs for backpressure 3) verify KV cache eviction and prefix cache hits 4) check autoscaling events. I'll run the cmds now.

ryan.oncall: logs show a cluster of 504 upstream errors from streaming-proxy pool (proxy-variant-b):
```
[2026-03-14T15:07:12Z] proxy-variant-b - upstream request timeout, id=xyz, code=504
[2026-03-14T15:07:13Z] proxy-variant-b - write failed: client closed connection
[2026-03-14T15:07:13Z] worker-42 - stalled while flushing chunk, kv_cache_hit=false
```

maria.sre: interesting — worker stalls on flush + client closed connections. that smells like client backpressure + proxy buffering (chunked stream not flushed) causing worker threads to block and queue up. p99 correlates with queue depth on workers.

elaine.devex: can we reproduce with a load test that simulates slow readers? I can spin a harness to open many slow SSE clients.

siva.eng: immediate mitigation options: - increase proxy upstream timeout to 30s (was 5s) - enable flush interval on proxy to force chunked frames through - scale streaming workers from 20 -> 60 - enable per-connection rate limiting to avoid single slow client exhausting worker sockets

ryan.oncall: doing controlled mitigations one at a time. first: bump upstream timeout and enable flush. applying to prod-us-west proxy pool now (patching config, no restart required for dynamic config). running:
```
# update envoy rate and flush settings
curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/proxy/pools/prod-us-west/patch -d '{"upstream_timeout":30000,"flush_interval_ms":100}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

incident-bot: deployment trigger: config-patch prod-us-west by ryan.oncall. CI check passed.

ryan.oncall: observing metrics... p99 down to 2.1s in 60s window. 504s dropping. still above SLO but trending down.

anya.support: notifying impacted customers list (shared doc). telling them we have a mitigation in place and will update in 30m.

maria.sre: second mitigation ready if needed: scale streaming-workers + restart proxy pool behind a rolling window to clear queued connections. planning a rolling restart of proxy-variant-b with drain-delay=10s. but prefer to avoid full restart if config patch holds.

ops-bot: autoscale event: streaming-workers increased from 20 -> 60 in prod-us-west (triggered by ryan.oncall).

siva.eng: I also rolled a hotfix to the runtime to avoid synchronous flush on main thread (candidate fix for stalls). it's staged on canary cluster. hash=b8d7c1. Not promoting until we confirm mitigations reduce pressure.

ryan.oncall: after scale + flush patch p99 is now ~0.95s in prod-us-west, p95 stable. prod-eu still at ~1.6s, applying same config patch there now.

elaine.devex: ran a quick slow-client test against canary to validate fix. with flush_interval=100ms, clients observe regular small chunks and server CPU stays healthy. test harness logs attached.

maria.sre: customer impact summary for pager: ~2% of streaming sessions experienced visible stalls >2s; top affected are EU region and mobile clients on flaky networks. no data loss; sessions recover after stall. recommend post-incident: 1) revert risky keepalive tweak from morning 2) add a new runbook for slow-client mitigation 3) increase default flush_interval for proxies for streaming endpoints 4) add alerts for worker queue depth and per-connection socket backlog.

ryan.oncall: handing off to maria.sre for follow-ups and RCA. I will remain reachable for 30m. handoff note: mitigations applied: proxy flush + upstream_timeout increase, workers scaled to 60, hotfix staged to canary.

maria.sre: taking over. next steps: coordinate with eng on promoting b8d7c1 hotfix after canary validation, schedule a targeted restart of proxy-variant-b in EU during low traffic window if config patch doesn't fully remediate, prepare postmortem draft with customer impact and timeline.

anya.support: will follow up with customers and update support tickets. request to marketing/product for templated messaging if needed.

siva.eng: I opened PR to revert the earlier keepalive tweak (PR #789). linking to postmortem once we have timeline.

maria.sre: marking incident as mitigated in the incident tracker. leaving this thread open for RCA notes. thanks everyone for fast responses. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: streaming.sse tail latency reduced below SLO in all regions. severity: sev2 -> monitoring. incident id: INC-2026-0314-76.

ryan.oncall: final note for handoff: commands and dashboards used during triage:
```
# dashboards
open https://grafana.redwood/streaming/slo?panel=p99
open https://grafana.redwood/streaming/worker-queues

# useful logs
logs stream --service proxy-variant-b --since 20m | grep "upstream request timeout"
```

maria.sre: capturing timeline and metrics for postmortem. will ping for review.

elaine.devex: writing a small playbook snippet for devs to test slow-reader behavior locally. will link in postmortem.

anya.support: customers updated. closing CX ticket after final confirmation.

ryan.oncall: logging out of oncall. good handoff. :wave:
